{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (1929–2023)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2023}}
[[File:Murre jacob.jpg|thumb|right|Murre in 2004]]
'''Jacob Pieter "Jaap" Murre''' (18 September 1929 – 9 April 2023) was a Dutch mathematician specializing in [[algebraic geometry]]. He was a professor of mathematics at [[Leiden University]] from 1961 to 1994.

==Career==
Murre was born on 18 September 1929 in [[Baarland]].<ref name=ul>{{cite web|author= |url=https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/1791 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602205344/https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/1791 |title=Jacob Pieter Murre |language=Dutch |publisher=Leiden University - Leidse hoogleraren vanaf 1575 |date= |archive-date=2 June 2020}}</ref> At his small primary school one of his classmates and friends was later botanist {{Interlanguage link multi|Jan Zeevaart|nl}}.<ref>{{cite web|author=Chris and Annie Peters |url=https://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~peters/teachers/Interview-JM-0812.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602214256/https://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~peters/teachers/Interview-JM-0812.pdf |title=Interview met Jaap Murre |language=Dutch |publisher=Institut Fourier |date=13 February 2012 |archive-date=2 June 2020}}</ref> Murre started studying mathematics at [[Delft University of Technology]] in 1947, he however switched to [[Leiden University]] where he obtained his degree in 1952.<ref name="memoriam">{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2023/04/in-memoriam---jaap-murre |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625151835/https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2023/04/in-memoriam---jaap-murre |title=In memoriam - professor Jaap Murre |language=Dutch |publisher=Leiden University |date=21 April 2023 |archive-date=25 June 2023}}</ref> With the [[Italian school of algebraic geometry]] being in fashion he was inspired by his promotor to do doctoral research under [[André Weil]] at the [[University of Chicago]], which he was able to do because of the [[Marshall Plan]].<ref name="memoriam"/> In 1957 Murre obtained his [[doctorate]] under [[Hendrik Kloosterman]] with a thesis titled: ''Over multipliciteiten van maximaal samenhangende bossen''.<ref name=ul/><ref name=cv>{{cite web|author= |url=http://pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~murrejp/cv.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230231414/http://pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~murrejp/cv.html |title=Curriculum Vitae Jacob Pieter Murre |publisher=Leiden University |date= |archive-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> By 1958 Murre became inspired by [[Alexander Grothendieck]] and managed to collaborate with him.<ref name="memoriam"/> In 1959 he was appointed associate professor (lector) at Leiden University. In 1961 he became professor of mathematics at the same institute, with a teaching assignment in [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name=ul/> [[Frans Oort]] was the first doctoral student he supervised, but Oort had to formally promote under Wil van Est as his promotion came one month before Murre's appointment.<ref name="memoriam"/> 

During his career Murre traveled frequently. He amongst others went to India to study with [[C. S. Seshadri]] and to the United Kingdom where he met [[David Mumford]], who inspired him to work on [[algebraic cycle]]s.<ref name="memoriam"/> In Italy he collaborated with {{ill|Alberto Conte|it}}, who became a friend. He also befriended American mathematician [[Spencer Bloch]]. In the 1990s he published on the [[Chow group]].<ref name="memoriam"/> Murre retired as professor in 1994.<ref name=cv/>

Murre was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1971.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4576 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200511191621/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4576 |title=Jaap Murre |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=11 May 2020}}</ref> In 2002 he obtained an honorary doctorate from the [[University of Turin]].<ref name="memoriam"/> Murre was elected a foreign member of the {{Interlanguage link multi|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|it}} in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.accademiadellescienze.it/accademia/soci/jacob-pietre-murre |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314170014/https://www.accademiadellescienze.it/accademia/soci/jacob-pietre-murre |title=Jacob Pietre MURRE |language=Italian |publisher=Accademia delle Scienze di Torino |date= |archive-date=14 March 2017}}</ref>

Murre died on 9 April 2023 at the age of 93.<ref name="memoriam"/>
